JUDGE BURST E1-judge-01 — four order-randomised A/B pairs of a fire projectile cast at a dummy in the painted cliffside scene, plus control (Run C-5, E1; charter § 4 E1: "four order-randomised A/B pairs (dirt, foliage, direction changes); ruling A / B / inconclusive (V13) / both fail (V18)"; JUDGE_RUBRIC.md; mechanical-process § 1 invariant 2: a known-bad control in every batch). task_id "E1-judge-02". You are a SEPARATE judging instance: you have not seen these effects built and you are not told which arm is which.

IMAGES: five boards (IMAGE 1–5). Each board shows the SAME cast twice, LEFT and RIGHT, as a strip of six frames at 1:1 from the real scene (cast → travel → contact → burst → residue) with the Keeper (146 px) for scale. The two sides differ only in how the projectile's travel is drawn. One of the five boards is a CONTROL whose two sides are byte-identical. Boards 1–5 are in random order; left/right is randomised per board.

For EACH board answer, in this exact JSON shape, one object per board: {"board": n, "prefer": "LEFT" | "RIGHT" | "SAME", "confidence": 0–1, "reads_as_painted": {"LEFT": true/false, "RIGHT": true/false}, "coherent_with_burst": {"LEFT": true/false, "RIGHT": true/false}, "notes": "≤ 40 words: what you saw, in the terms of the rubric — hand-drawn contour, flat planes, no gradient haze; the travel body must read as the SAME fire as the burst it ends in"}. "SAME" is a legitimate answer and is expected for exactly one board. Do not guess a preference where you see none.

Return ONLY the receipt (task_id "E1-judge-02") with files = [] and images = 0 (INTEGER), calls_used, and the JSON array above under self_report.judgements; status DELIVERED. No image generation. No web. No code.
